nodes.label: Test Frame 00097 - Peak-Density Flock (IPC-Siren, 2022-02-26 23:11:16)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the held-out test split showing the highest stocking density of the six frames - mid-size broilers blanket the upper two-thirds of the floor with heavy mutual occlusion and touching body outlines. All five pan feeders visibly contain pale feed. A cleared band of bare litter runs across the lower third below the feed line.
nodes.rationale: The crowding here makes instance boundaries ambiguous, which is exactly the regime where counting/detection error concentrates - a deliberate stress case for the evaluation split.

nodes.label: High Stocking Density and Mutual Occlusion
nodes.description: The condition in which birds tile the floor with touching or overlapping silhouettes so that individual instance boundaries are not recoverable from a single frame and the flock reads as continuous white texture rather than as countable objects.
nodes.rationale: This sets the practical ceiling on per-bird detection accuracy and is the main argument for treating the problem as density estimation or region-level behaviour scoring rather than exhaustive individual instance counting.

nodes.label: img/ Versus img_test/ Directory Split Convention
nodes.description: The dataset partitions frames by directory rather than by manifest file: img/ holds the training frames and img_test/ holds the evaluation frames, each using an independent frameNNNNN.png numbering series that restarts from zero.
nodes.rationale: Directory-based splitting is simple and tool-agnostic, but here both directories draw on the same camera and overlapping calendar dates, so the partition does not by itself guarantee that train and test frames are independent samples.
